g.text: Roofline Model: why decode is memory-bound and prefill is compute-bound
Explained on: session 08 FlashAttention · session 02 (memory math) | P = min(P_compute, AI x BW)
1. Two hardware ceilings joined by arithmetic intensity
high AI = much math per byte
P = min( P_compute , AI x BW )
Slope of the left side = memory bandwidth
Keep AI >= ridge to use all the FLOPs.
2. The whole thing in one table (toy GPU: 100 TFLOPS, 500 GB/s)
achieved TFLOPS (bar length = 3 px per TFLOPS)
AI > 200 -> raise compute or cut FLOPs
AI = 2000 is NOT 10x faster than AI = 200:
both already sit on the 100 TFLOPS roof.
You want ENOUGH AI to reach the roof,
3. The roofline drawn (log-log): toy GPU vs real A100 and H100
Even MQA (AI=32) reaches only 32/200 = 16% of the
A100 ridge: decode attention stays memory-bound.
so the same HBM feeds more FLOPs per second.
New GPUs add FLOPs faster than bandwidth ->
ridge rises -> decode gets MORE memory-bound.
AI = 50 -> P = 50 x 1.8 = 90 TFLOPS (9% of peak).
4. Why decode attention is memory-bound: AI = H_q / H_kv
ONE LAYER, ONE NEW TOKEN, CONTEXT T
(read K and V for every cached token)
bar length = AI x 8 px; ridge = 200 -> would be 1600 px
Even the most aggressive sharing leaves decode
GQA's win = fewer BYTES (and VRAM), not a
Weight GEMV in decode (batch B tokens):
Batching raises AI: it reuses each weight read.
5. Batching rescues weight matmuls: AI = B (A100: ridge 200, roof 312 TFLOPS)
ceiling = min(312, B x 1.555 TFLOPS); bar length = 2 px per TFLOPS
This is why continuous batching raises GPU
utilisation, but the KV cache of each request
is NOT shared, so attention AI never grows with B.
TRADE-OFF: batching needs B x KV bytes of VRAM
compute, caps B in long-context serving.
6. Two completely different cases: how to remove each bottleneck
mem could feed 1000 x 500 = 500 TFLOPS; GPU has 100
TPOT down 16x (T term); bytes AND FLOPs
both /16, so attention AI stays H_q/H_kv
roof doubles, AI=1000 still on roof
ridge. Do NOT pay quality for it.
AI < ridge => attack the MEMORY bottleneck
AI > ridge => attack the COMPUTE bottleneck
You want enough AI to hit the roof, not max AI:
AI=200 and AI=2000 both reach 100 TFLOPS.
7. GPU A vs GPU B: you cannot answer without AI
Decode (AI ~ 1..30) lives far left of both ridges:
8. LLM inference: prefill vs decode on the roofline
1 new token -> Q, read KV cache
GQA/MQA, KV quantization, paged KV, sliding window,
Metrics: prefill -> TTFT (time to first token); decode -> TPOT (time per output token)
